related_questions.question: Do US citizens need a visa for the EU?

text_blocks.snippet: No, US citizens do not need a visa for the EU for short stays (usually up to 90 days) for tourism or business purposes. However, starting in late 2026, they will need to apply for an electronic travel authorization called ETIAS before traveling to most EU countries according to the U.S. Department of State (.gov).
snippet_highlighted_words: No, US citizens do not need a visa for the EU for short stays (usually up to 90 days) for tourism or business purposes

list.title: Current Situation:
list.snippet: US citizens can currently travel to most EU countries for up to 90 days without a visa.

list.title: ETIAS:
list.snippet: The European Travel Information and Authorization System (ETIAS) is a new electronic system that will be implemented in the last quarter of 2026.

list.title: What ETIAS Means:
list.snippet: Once ETIAS is in effect, US citizens will need to apply for authorization through the ETIAS system before their trip.

list.title: How to Apply:
list.snippet: The ETIAS application will be available online and will require basic information, passport details, travel plans, and potentially information about past travel to conflict zones or criminal convictions.

list.title: ETIAS is not a visa:
list.snippet: It's a travel authorization system that allows visa-exempt countries to enter the EU for short stays.

list.title: Cost:
list.snippet: The ETIAS application is expected to cost 7 euros for travelers between 18 and 70 years old.

list.title: Exemptions:
list.snippet: Travelers under 18 or over 70 will not be required to pay the ETIAS fee.

list.title: Other Requirements:
list.snippet: Even with ETIAS, US citizens may need to apply for a visa if they plan to stay longer than 90 days or if they intend to work or study in the EU.

list.title: Specific Countries:
list.snippet: ETIAS will apply to most EU countries, but not all. For example, Ireland is not part of the Schengen Area and has its own visa requirements according to a Reddit thread.
